name: Sarclet Harbour (zircon RS-ORS-18-17)
note: Strachan et al. 2021: reddish lithic arkose, Lower ORS. KS p=0.865 (replication). Thermal: local Ro 3.1–4.7% (Hillier & Marshall 1992) vs the Altar Stone's R1-ordered illite/smectite with ~20% expandability, whereas I/S in Caithness and Orkney is <10% expandable (Pirrie et al. 2026) — this clay contrast, not a measured Ro on the stone, drives the fail; only 0-score among candidates.
cite: L7 fail: measured Ro 3.1–4.7% at Sarclet (Hillier & Marshall 1992 Figs 2–4: Lybster, Hillhead, Clyth) vs the Altar Stone's illite/smectite with ~20% expandability, whereas I/S in Caithness and Orkney is <10% expandable (Pirrie et al. 2026, after Hillier & Clayton 1989; Hillier & Marshall 1992). The Altar Stone's own Ro is not measured; a ≲1% Ro-equivalent is Daw's inference (sarsen.org, 11 Jul 2026), not a figure from Bevins et al. or Pirrie et al. Zircon comparison: Clarke et al. (2026).

name: Castletown Quarry CS037P (measured Sr)
note: Mey Subgroup, Upper Caithness Flagstone Group (Facies B). Lab XRF whole rock: Sr 406 ppm, CaO 7.37% (Ba 473 ppm). Sr/Ca 7.7×10⁻³. Fails the Sr ceiling at 160, 200 and 250 ppm, and Sr/Ca at every cut-off. Ba below the 1025 ppm floor. Reference locality added for the Sr layers; L3–L8 not assessed here. Handheld vs lab: Altar Stone Sr is pXRF on weathered/cut surfaces (~2 mm information depth); Caithness Sr is lab XRF on powders.

name: Dounreay Borehole 1 flagstones (measured Sr)
note: Caithness Flagstone Group (Dounreay Shore and Sandside Bay Fms), n = 29 lab XRF: Sr 131–1388 ppm, median 415. Only 2, 3 and 5 of 29 pass at 160, 200 and 250 ppm, so the place fails. The few exceptions are low-carbonate sandstones/siltstones (A146 132, A151 131, A152 165; plus A158 240 and A160 237 at 250; CaO ≤7.9%), unlike the calcite-cemented Altar Stone. Sr/Ca 3.8–9.6×10⁻³ (all 37 Devonian samples 3.8–18.9, median ~7): every sample fails Sr/Ca. Reference locality added for the Sr layers; L3–L8 not assessed here. Handheld vs lab: Altar Stone Sr is pXRF on weathered/cut surfaces (~2 mm information depth); Caithness Sr is lab XRF on powders.

name: Stenness & Brodgar standing stones, Orkney (measured Sr)
note: Bevins et al. 2024 pXRF on the Stones of Stenness and Ring of Brodgar (local Stromness flagstone): Sr from around 400 ppm up to 1260 ppm. Fails the Sr ceiling at every cut-off. The source wording is ambiguous (the same 1260 figure is also given for Brodgar Ba); check against the Bevins et al. 2024 pXRF supplement. Sr/Ca untested (no Ca in the text). Already excluded by Bevins et al. on Ba/Rb/K. Marker placed between the two monuments. Handheld vs lab: Altar Stone Sr is pXRF on weathered/cut surfaces (~2 mm information depth); Caithness Sr is lab XRF on powders.
